desc: Establish that an optimal set of \(k\) pairs can use the \(k\) smallest mochi as bottoms and the \(k\) largest mochi as tops, matched in order.
Reduce feasibility of \(k\) pairs in \([L,R]\) to \(\operatorname{lower\_bound}(2A_i)\le R-k+1+i-L\) for every \(i\in[L,R-k]\).
Reformulate feasibility using \(B_i=\operatorname{lower\_bound}(2A_i)-i\), giving \(\max B_i\) on a range and threshold \((R-L+1)-k\).
Build an RMQ sparse table over \(B\), and binary-search the largest feasible \(k\) for each query.
Prove monotonicity of the feasibility predicate in \(k\), including duplicates and \(k=0\).
Write the Python solution with fast I/O and confirm it passes both public samples with the required complexity.
